title: DIY Herb‑Spiced Butter for Grilled Corn on the Cob Using Scissors
meta_description: Elevate your BBQ with this easy herb spiced butter for grilled corn. Learn how to use herb scissors to prep fresh toppings in seconds.
html:
There is nothing quite like the smell of corn roasting over an open flame during a summer barbecue, but plain butter simply doesn't do it justice anymore. If you want to elevate your side dish game and impress your guests, the secret is undoubtedly herb spiced butter grilled corn. It adds a burst of freshness and complexity that pairs perfectly with the smoky, charred flavor of the corn. The best part? You don't need to be a chef to pull this off. You just need the right ingredients and a clever tool to make prep work a breeze.

Selecting the Best Herbs for Flavor

When you are building your butter compound, the choice of herbs defines the personality of the dish. For a classic, bright profile that cuts through the richness of the butter, cilantro and chives are unbeatable. Cilantro offers a citrusy zest that works wonders with the sweetness of the corn, while chives provide a mild onion flavor that isn't overpowering. If you prefer a more savory, Italian-inspired route, fresh basil is the way to go. Whichever direction you choose, fresh is non-negotiable here. Dried herbs won't provide the vibrant color or the punchy taste required for the best herb spiced butter grilled corn experience.

Why Use Herb Scissors?

Chopping tiny herbs like cilantro or chives with a traditional knife can be tedious. Often, you end up crushing the leaves rather than cutting them, or they stick to your blade in a frustrating clump. This is where having the right gadget changes everything. I keep a pair of Herb Scissors in my drawer specifically for this task. These five-blade herb shears mince cilantro, chives, and basil in one snip, giving you uniform pieces that look professional and cook evenly.

Unlike a single knife blade, these shears act as multiple knives working at once, drastically reducing your prep time. They are especially useful when you are prepping for a crowd and need a large volume of herbs quickly. Plus, because herbs often get stuck between the blades, the fact that this set comes with a cleaning comb is a lifesaver. A quick swipe of the comb clears the blades, so you don't have to pick green bits out by hand.

Preparing the Herb Spiced Butter

The foundation of any good compound butter is the butter itself. You want to use unsalted butter so you can control the sodium level, but salted works in a pinch if you adjust your seasoning accordingly. Ensure the butter is at room temperature; it should be soft enough to squish between your fingers but not melted. This texture allows the herbs and spices to disperse evenly without separating.

For this recipe, we will focus on a savory, zesty blend that complements almost any grilled meat. Use your Herb Scissors to snip the cilantro and chives directly over the butter bowl. This catches all the flavorful juices that might otherwise escape on a cutting board.

  1. Soften the Butter: Place 1 stick (1/2 cup) of room-temperature unsalted butter in a medium mixing bowl.
  2. Mince the Herbs: Using your Herb Scissors, snip 2 tablespoons of fresh cilantro and 1 tablespoon of fresh chives directly over the butter.
  3. Add Seasoning: Add 1 teaspoon of smoked paprika (for that grilled essence), 1/2 teaspoon of garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon of lime zest, and salt and pepper to taste.
  4. Mix Thoroughly: Use a fork to mash and mix everything together until the herbs are evenly distributed and the butter turns a vibrant greenish-orange hue.
  5. Shape and Chill: Scoop the mixture onto a sheet of parchment paper, roll it into a log, and twist the ends. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to firm up.

Grilling the Corn to Perfection

Now that your butter is ready, it is time to focus on the corn. Soaking the corn in the husk for about 15 minutes before grilling adds moisture and prevents the husks from burning instantly. However, for maximum char flavor, I recommend peeling back the husks and removing the silk, then pulling the husks back up to cover the ear. This acts as a natural handle while protecting the kernels slightly.

Preheat your grill to medium-high heat, around 375°F to 400°F. Place the corn on the grates, turning occasionally. Once the husks are charred and the kernels feel tender to the touch—usually about 10 to 15 minutes—remove them from the heat. Peel back the husks to use as a handle for eating. While the corn is still hot, slice a coin of your herb spiced butter and place it on top. The residual heat will melt the butter, carrying the cilantro, lime, and smoked paprika deep into every kernel.

FAQ

Can I use this butter for other vegetables?

Absolutely. This compound butter is fantastic on grilled zucchini, steamed potatoes, or even melted over a grilled steak. The combination of smoked paprika and fresh herbs pairs well with almost any savory dish.

How should I clean sticky residue off the shears?

Herb scissors can get gummy because of the plant resins in fresh herbs. It is best to rinse them immediately after use in warm, soapy water. Use the included cleaning comb to scrape between the blades to ensure no bits are left behind before washing.

Can I freeze the herb butter log?

Yes, compound butter freezes beautifully. Wrap the parchment-wrapped log tightly in a layer of plastic wrap or foil and store it in the freezer for up to three months. You can slice off a round whenever you need it, straight from the freezer.
